transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Karen (Redwood SE), Maya, Evan, Priya (Lyra)

Summary: 4-week POC to validate latency, throughput and unit cost for product recommendation inference. Focus on integration options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security controls, and executive readout at end of pilot.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we figured half hour to 45 so we can cover success criteria and the timeline. um, quick intros, karen and i from Redwood.
[00:18] Maya: hi, maya here. head of ML at Lyra. excited to scope this out, we have a live recommender that needs better tail latency and lower per-request cost.
[00:30] Evan: evan, cto. primary concerns: latency under load, customer data never leaving region, and easy rollback if quality degrades.
[00:45] Karen: great, we'll run through what a typical 4-week POC looks like, the benchmarks we recommend, and the access we need. quick note - our product names sometimes get munged in transcripts, but Redwood Dedicated = reserved capacity, Redwood Private = VPC/on-prem option.
[01:05] Priya: on security side i'll own the network and service account setup, also will need SOC2 and KMS details.
[01:18] Karen: perfect. success criteria - can we make sure these align with what you expect?
[01:25] Maya: yes, here's what we care about: 95th percentile latency < 200ms for 512 token responses, tail under 300ms at 95th under our 200rps simulated load, accuracy within 1% of current model's recommendation recall, and per-1000 requests cost less than $X (we discussed target offline).
[01:45] Samir: okay that's very actionable. we'll break that down into measurable benchmarks. for throughput, we'll run a 200rps steady load and a burst test up to 500rps for short windows. we'll report p50/p95/p99 and tokenized cost.
[02:10] Evan: do you need full user data or can we run on anonymized feature vectors?
[02:18] Karen: anonymized vectors are fine as long as they exercise the same distribution. sample schema + 72 hrs of traffic or a representative day's traffic should be enough for the bench.
[02:35] Maya: we can provide three days of anonymized traffic; will that be sufficient?
[02:40] Karen: yes. also please include sequence length distribution - we care about the KV cache hit rates, prefix reuse etc.
[02:55] Priya: any special network requirements for Redwood hosted? we prefer dedicated for production but for POC hosted is fine if data stays in eu-west and encryption in transit+at rest with customer keys.
[03:10] Samir: we can do a hosted pilot in eu-west, with option to move to dedicated or private if you want to test VPC peering. for KMS we support customer-managed keys, and we'll share SOC2 and KMS notes after the call.
[03:30] Evan: timeline - what's realistic to get useful numbers?
[03:36] Karen: our recommended milestone cadence for this POC: kickoff and access/setup (week 0), run baseline benchmarks and integration (week 1), mid-point review with preliminary numbers and any tuning (end of week 2), iterative runs and cost tuning (week 3), exec readout + handoff + next steps (end of week 4).
[03:58] Maya: so 4 weeks total, good. can you outline the deliverables per milestone?
[04:05] Karen: yes - kickoff: access, sample data ingest, run quick sanity tests. week 1: baseline numbers (latency, throughput, quality), initial optimizations (batching, quantization suggestions). week 2 mid-point: share detailed report comparing to your internal baseline and suggested config changes. week 3: run tuned benchmarks and cost analysis. week 4: exec readout deck and recommended deployment path (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and an SLA recommendation.
[04:38] Samir: we'll include a short runbook for rollback and fallback policies; e.g., automatic fallback to smaller model variant if latency spikes.
[04:46] Evan: what's typical infra for the dedicated option? GPUs?
[04:50] Karen: depends on model size, but we usually use A100/ultrascale or equivalent, and we provide kernels and quantization profiles. for POC we'll estimate instance class after we see model size and sequence lengths.
[05:05] Priya: regarding compliance, can you confirm audit logs and SSO?
[05:10] Samir: yes - RBAC, SAML/SSO integrations, detailed audit logs retained per your retention policy; we'll send the SOC2 and IS0 docs and an audit log sample.
[05:22] Maya: benchmarks - what exactly will you measure?
[05:26] Karen: latencies (p50/p95/p99), throughput under steady state, burst behavior, tokenized cost per 1k requests, model output quality via recall/precision on your eval set, and regression testing versus your baseline prompts. we'll also report on cache hit rates (KV cache), batching efficiency, and suggestion for quantization level if acceptable.
[06:00] Evan: one question on quality - if Redwood's optimizations change outputs slightly, how do we evaluate?
[06:07] Karen: we'll run side-by-side evals on your labeled set. goal is within your tolerance (you mentioned 1% recall drop). if beyond that we'll tune batching/quantization or fall back to a higher-precision variant for production.
[06:25] Maya: curious about benchmarking time - how long does each run take?
[06:29] Karen: depends, but a full suite across multiple loads usually completes in a day once data is ingested; initial sanity runs take an hour or two.
[06:40] Samir: costs - we'll provide a pilot estimate and then a forecast for production at target throughput. you asked for unit cost under $X per 1k; we'll model several scenarios.
[06:55] Priya: networking and VPC peering - if we need private, what do you need from us?
[07:01] Karen: for VPC peering we need network CIDR, peering window, and a firewall rule list. Priya, we can share a checklist after the call.
[07:10] Maya: ok, next steps recap?
[07:14] Samir: i'll send the SOW and pilot pricing by tomorrow (2026-09-10). Karen will share the benchmark template and ingestion script. Maya will provide sample traffic. Priya will start network checklist. we'll tentatively schedule kickoff for 2026-09-13.
[07:30] Evan: that works for us. also please include a short exec deck template for the readout.
[07:36] Karen: yes we'll include an exec summary slide with key metrics and recommended deployment path.
[07:45] Maya: any known blockers?
[07:47] Samir: the main blocker is sample data access and network setup for private tests; otherwise we can run hosted benchmarks quickly.
[07:56] Priya: i'll prioritize the service account and firewall notes.
[08:00] Samir: great. thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.

Recap (spoken): agreed success criteria: p95 < 200ms / quality within 1% recall / cost target. Milestones: kickoff (access & sanity), week1 baseline, week2 mid-point review, week3 tuning & cost runs, week4 exec readout. Deliverables: bench reports, exec deck, runbook, security docs.

Links mentioned: POC SOW (to be sent), benchmark template (to be shared), SOC2 & KMS docs (to be shared).

End of transcript.
